text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT AND SOYBEAN SALE - A Philippine food manufacturer and flour miller bought 17,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for mid-November shipment, traders said on Friday. The firm also bought 6,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans at over $200 per tonne FOB from an American commodity house Thursday night, they said.

WHEAT TENDER - Egypt's official commodities buyer was seeking 50,000 tonnes of American soft red or soft white wheat for loading from Nov 18-30. Egypt tendered earlier this week for 50,000 tonnes of Australian soft white wheat or French soft red wheat. The deadline for American bids was Saturday.

- Traders said on Friday a second Philippine firm advised commodity houses that it was in the market for 23,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, bringing the total local requirement to 35,000 tonnes. Earlier today, traders said another Philippine firm asked for price quotations for 12,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for November shipment.

WHEAT TENDER - Pakistan is seeking 200,000 tonnes of U.S. number two or better soft white wheat for November 12-30 delivery, the buyers' U.S. agent said. Bids will be opened on November 3 at 1100 local time and must remain valid until 1800 local time the following day.
CORN TENDER - The Philippine state National Food Authority said on Friday it would tender for 150,000 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn No 2 or its equivalent on October 29.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - The Egyptian state's Food Industries Company said on Wednesday it was extending until noon (1000 GMT) on November 6 the deadline for bids for 30,000 tonnes U.S. or Argentine yellow corn and 30,000 tonnes of soybeans, any origin. The old deadline was October 30.
BARLEY TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission said it invited tenders by October 29 for 25,000 tonnes feed barley for Nov 20-Dec 5 shipment from Europe or Nov 10-25 from North America.

MARKET TALK - Recent talk in the Brazilian market that crushers have been buying U.S. soybeans may be linked to export sales to unknown destinations reported today by the U.S. Department of Agriculture. The latest USDA report included 331,600 tonnes sold to unknown destinations in the week to October 17 which led to speculation in Chicago that Brazil may have been a buyer of a substantial proportion of the total.

... U.S. rice exports to Asia look promising especially if Japan and South Korea honor market liberalization commitments, a USDA agricultural economist said. U.S. rice exports in 1996 to Japan will probably hit around 450,000 tonnes while South Korea is expected to reach about 100,000 tonnes.

... Egypt's main commodities buyer Samir el-Shakankiri denied rumors that he had bought 1.2 million bushels of Australian wheat overnight. "We have not bought such a large amount of Australian wheat. This news is not true."
